works.version: Ronald W. Wolff, Operations Research 30 (1982) 223–231, DOI 10.1287/opre.30.2.223, JSTOR publisher scan
scope: PDF 1 JSTOR wrapper; 2–4 examples and lack-of-anticipation assumption; 5–7 martingale convergence proof; 7–10 nonstationary extension, converse and references.

PDF 4 printed 225 states the lack-of-anticipation assumption and conditional long-run equality. PDF 5 printed 226 relates expected counts to integrated time and starts the proof. Section 3 uses rate-weighted time for nonstationary arrivals.
works.gap: The event stream and pre-arrival state must meet the theorem assumptions. Event selections or independent loss factors do not follow from the equality.

scope: PDF 1–2 LENDA and digital acquisition; 2–4 filter, interpolation and split-pulse/detector tests; 4–6 light output, neutron response and synchronization.

PDF 2–3 Eqs. (2)–(4) records filter and interpolation; PDF 3–4 Eq. (5) and Fig. 4 separate the two-bar timing difference from the high-light single-bar timing near 400 ps under the assumed resolution scaling.
works.gap: Energy thresholds and timing depend on the tested detector, light output and geometry. This is one detector calibration and not a general timing law.

works.gap: The high-K response and axis have specified configuration, pairing and frame. The spectral estimate is not a freely interchangeable ground-band moment.
